clue.text: Ancient Greek coin's condition, right?

definitions.note: read as 'Ancient Greek coin is', the 's working as a link

parts.note: a condition or situation is a state, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A coin collector asks whether an ancient Greek coin is in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'coin' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver piece minted in the city-states of classical Greece.

clue.text: Sirens unfortunately without spirit

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
rum is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: Sadly the sirens are sounding with no spirit behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: RUM sits inside ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarums is an old word for warning calls or alarms, the job a siren does.

clue.text: Assumed to have worked as a nurse before

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a nurse tends patients, so she tended them

explanation.surface: Someone took on a role, having previously worked as a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a manner or air is to feign it, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Setting the pace over exercise, that's plain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: to set the pace in a dance or march is to step it out
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A coach setting the pace in a workout says that's plain enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland, a kind of plain found in Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: A non-drinker almost all ache to join

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

indicators.note: almost all of the word means it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A teetotaller who aches nearly everywhere wants to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach things is to fasten or connect them, a synonym.

clue.text: Put a diet to rights and fitness results

indicators.note: putting something to rights means sorting it out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Correct your diet and you will get fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is part of the fodder as well as the start of the phrase 'put to rights'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitude is natural suitability or fitness for a task.

clue.text: Issue two together

parts.note: issue means offspring: children born as a pair at one birth

explanation.surface: Instructions to publish two things at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of babies born at the same birth are offspring, issue, arriving together.

clue.text: The washer the college-head tips with little hesitation

parts.note: the head, first letter, of college is C
to tip over is to lean
er is the small sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: The head of a college hesitantly tips the man who does the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is a product used for washing skin or surfaces.

clue.text: Allow the French following to dress down

indicators.note: the French article comes after, following, the word to

parts.note: le is French for the
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Being told off is permitted by the French rules that follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate' in the old sense means to scold, the same as 'dress down'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to put up with or permit it.

clue.text: A musician breaking down in tears

indicators.note: breaking something down splits its letters to be reassembled

explanation.surface: A performer collapses weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer was a Victorian English composer and organist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was a composer and organist at St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: One of a pack Jack will have to return

parts.note: a jack tar, or just tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: to return is to turn back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A card player says Jack will have to go back to the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards come in a deck used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Supporters of quiet technicians

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical term for quietly
artisans are skilled craftsmen

explanation.surface: Fans of silent craftspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisans are committed followers who back a cause.

clue.text: Provide weapons for a body of servicemen

definitions.meaning: a branch of the ... forces, as in the air branch

explanation.definitionFit: To equip troops with weapons, and a division of the armed services such as the Fleet Air one.

clue.text: A suggestion to do with understanding by the queen

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with
mind means intellect, understanding
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen offers a hint about comprehension.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt that jogs someone's memory is a nudge or hint.

clue.text: How an Australian gets rigged out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: How a man from Down Under gets kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: Digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Digger is a colloquial name for an Australian, from the gold-diggers and soldiers of the First World War.

clue.text: Not recognised under the new title?

definitions.text: Not recognised under the new title?

parts.words: Not recognised under the new title?
parts.note: someone travelling under an assumed name is unknown to others

explanation.surface: Someone who has changed their name goes unrecognised.
explanation.definitionFit: Going about in disguise or under a false name means concealing one's identity.

clue.text: They'll get the leavings

parts.note: leavings suggests scraps, but means what someone leaves in a will

explanation.surface: Those who get the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Legatees are people who receive bequests under a will.

clue.text: See some likely advantages

indicators.note: some of the word means just a part of it is taken

explanation.surface: Spot some probable benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a noun: a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a diocese with its own cathedral, a bishop's seat.

clue.text: Sound guy in some craft

parts.note: sound means measure water depth, with a weighted line from a boat

explanation.surface: An audio technician working in a particular trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A leadsman takes soundings with a lead line from a ship's side.

clue.text: Write, subject to restrictions

explanation.definitionFit: To set down words on paper, and to shut animals in an enclosure.

clue.text: Clarify a letter about cash on delivery

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, one piece going round another

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the fourth letter

explanation.surface: Explain a note concerning payment on receipt.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to make its meaning plain.

clue.text: Capital protection, in whatever form

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the following word

explanation.surface: Safeguarding money whatever shape it takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Headwear shields the head, and capital comes from Latin caput, head.

clue.text: A fortune-teller, one taking his evening meal about six

indicators.note: the diner stands round, about, the number

parts.note: a diner is someone eating dinner
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant sits down to supper around six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A diviner foretells the future or finds hidden things by supernatural means.

clue.text: The antisocial guy who's fired

parts.note: fired suggests sacked, but means one who sets things alight

explanation.surface: A troublesome worker has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately sets buildings alight commits a criminal fire-raising offence.

clue.text: Communist admitting copy will be cut

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: red is a standard term for a communist
to ape is to imitate, copy

explanation.surface: A party member letting in a plagiarist faces censorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops are reaped when they are harvested, mown down.

clue.text: Stylish attempt to encompass an objective

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A fashionable effort to take in a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fashionable follows the latest style.

clue.text: Frank scoffed, though he wanted the job

parts.note: frank means open, candid
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Frank ate greedily even though he was hoping for the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant for a post is someone who wanted it.

clue.text: A man who wrote of capsizing in the river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one in Wales and England

indicators.note: capsizing turns over, so in a down clue the little word is turned upside down

explanation.surface: A writer describes a boat overturning in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, a story of shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist behind Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: One is creating pandemonium

indicators.note: creating suggests making something new from these letters

explanation.surface: A single person is making chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or racket is the sound of uproar.

clue.text: The odour given by smoke

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
fume is smoke or vapour

explanation.surface: The smell produced by smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume is a pleasant scent, a fragrant smell.

clue.text: In time past a farm-hand read, then worked

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters are kneaded into a new shape

explanation.surface: Long ago a farm labourer read, then went to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A neatherd was a cowherd: neat is an archaic word for cattle.

clue.text: Like an aquatic bird's back

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Something resembles the rear end of a waterbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the rear of a ship, behind.
